title: Four drain points: reverse order and error isolation
wave: Wave 1 — Lifecycle foundation (W1, W2, W3, W5)
one_line: Add one shared `drainDisposers` helper that runs registered teardown callbacks last-registered-first, keeps going when one throws (logging instead of rethrowing), and repeats until the list is empty — then route all four existing drain loops through it.
user_visible_effect: none directly — internal hardening. A throwing extension teardown callback (or a settings unsubscribe that throws during a config reload) can no longer abort the rest of session shutdown, so a `Ctrl-C` / `/exit` no longer risks leaking a draft save, background bash jobs, or the extension `session_shutdown` event. Manifests in `~/.omp/logs/omp.YYYY-MM-DD.log` gain a `Disposer threw during drain` warn line that a crash report would not have carried before.
effort: S — one ~15-line helper, four one-line call-site swaps, three import lines, one ~70-line test file, one changelog line.
risk: The single most likely way to get this wrong is porting chord's `throw errors[0]` / `AggregateError` shape. The drain is a synchronous contract called by `beginDispose()`, which `session-teardown.ts:70` invokes BEFORE the `try` that wraps `await deps.saveDraft(draftText)`. A throwing drain would reject the teardown promise before the draft is written, converting a conditional leak into an unconditional one — the exact outcome the surrounding doc comment says the design exists to prevent. The second-most-likely mistake is a splice-once implementation, which silently drops disposers registered while teardown is running; `agent-session.ts:5217` documents a second drain pass that exists solely to catch those.

steps.instruction: Create the helper using the code_shape below. Use `Array.prototype.pop()` in a `while (list.length > 0)` loop rather than `splice(0)` + reverse-iterate: pop gives strict last-registered-first ordering for free, mutates the caller's array in place so the existing call sites need no assignment, and drains to empty with no outer retry loop — a disposer that pushes a new disposer mid-drain is picked up on the very next iteration. Wrap each call in try/catch and report through `logger.warn` with the error stringified via `String(error)`, matching the `logger.warn("...", { error: String(err) })` shape used throughout `session-teardown.ts` and `agent-session.ts`. The function must have no code path that rethrows.

Replace the line `for (const dispose of this.#disposers.splice(0)) dispose();` with `drainDisposers(this.#disposers);`. It sits as the second statement of `beginDispose()` (which opens at 4981), immediately after `this.#isDisposed = true;` and before `this.#modelDiscoveryAbortController.abort();`. Do not reorder anything else in that method — the surrounding statements are a deliberate ordering of teardown guards.

Replace the second, identical line `for (const dispose of this.#disposers.splice(0)) dispose();` with `drainDisposers(this.#disposers);`. It is directly under the comment `// beginDispose() drained the rest; this catches registrations made during teardown.` (line 5217) — keep that comment, it is the reason the pass exists. This is the pass that makes the drain-to-empty loop observable; a splice-once helper would make this line dead code.

Replace `for (const dispose of this.#fileFallbackDisposers.splice(0)) dispose();` — the entire body of `disposeFileFallbacks()` — with `drainDisposers(this.#fileFallbackDisposers);`. Keep the method's existing JSDoc (it explains the process-wide registry rationale).

Replace `for (const dispose of this.#composerShapeDisposers.splice(0)) dispose();` — the entire body of `disposeComposerShapes()` — with `drainDisposers(this.#composerShapeDisposers);`. Do NOT touch `#dialogQueue` (line 93) or `#extensionTerminalInputUnsubscribers` (line 85) — see open_questions.

Add `import { drainDisposers } from "../utils/disposers";`. Extensionless relative specifier, no `.js`, matching lines 250-255. In `runner.ts` add `import { drainDisposers } from "../../utils/disposers";` into the `../../` block (after line 30, `../../tools/file-write-fallback`). In `extension-ui-controller.ts` add `import { drainDisposers } from "../../utils/disposers";` next to the existing `../../utils/*` imports at lines 36-37. All three are top-level static imports — no dynamic import, per AGENTS.md.

Write the three tests from the test_contract. Order of registration in the order test must be A, B, C and the assertion is the reverse run order C, B, A — the assertion is the point, so build the run list with a `calls: string[]` push from each closure and assert `calls` deep-equals `["C", "B", "A"]`. The isolation test must register the throwing disposer LAST (so, under reverse order, it runs FIRST) and assert the earlier-registered disposer still ran — that is the exact failure mode. The two-round test must have one disposer push a new disposer into the same array when it runs, then assert the array is empty afterwards, not merely that the first round ran. Use `vi.spyOn(logger, "warn").mockImplementation(() => {})` and `vi.restoreAllMocks()` in `afterEach` — never `mock.module()`, which leaks across files (bun#12823). Do not source-grep the implementation file.
Add a `### Fixed` subsection directly under `## [Unreleased]` (line 3) with one user-facing line. Do not touch the `## [18.3.3]` section — released sections are immutable.

Run `bun install` first (node_modules is absent in this checkout — see plan_corrections), then `bun run check:ts`, then `bun test packages/coding-agent/test/disposer-drain.test.ts`. If the test file turns out to require the unbuilt native addon, that is a regression against the expectation recorded in open_questions and should be reported rather than worked around.

test_contract:
The contract is: "draining disposers runs them last-registered-first, a disposer that throws neither stops the ones after it nor escapes the drain, and a disposer registered during the drain still runs." Three tests, one per clause, all asserting on an observable `string[]` run-order array or on `logger.warn` being called — never on internal wiring.

(1) `runs disposers in reverse registration order` — register A, B, C (in that order), drain, assert `calls` deep-equals `["C", "B", "A"]`. Consumer-visible failure: a forward-order drain would leave a resource acquired by A still live when B's teardown runs — the leak this milestone exists to close. This is the assertion most likely to fail on a first attempt, because the current code is forward-order at all four sites.

(2) `a throwing disposer does not stop later disposers and is logged` — register a non-throwing disposer first, then a throwing one (so reverse order runs the thrower first), drain. Assert (a) the non-throwing disposer still ran, (b) `drainDisposers` itself did not throw, and (c) `logger.warn` was called exactly once. Consumer-visible failure: without the try/catch, the throwing disposer aborts the loop and the listener teardown registered before it never runs, leaking a live settings watcher against a disposed session; without the logger call, the failure is silent and a user reports "omp hung on exit" with nothing in the log.

(3) `drains disposers registered during the drain` — one disposer pushes a second disposer into the same array when it runs; drain; assert the array is EMPTY afterwards and the late disposer ran. Consumer-visible failure: a splice-once helper leaves the array non-empty and the late disposer never runs — which is precisely what `agent-session.ts:5217`'s second pass exists to catch. Asserting only that the first round ran would let that bug ship.

Not covered, and deliberately so: the exact `logger.warn` message text, the number of drain rounds, and any assertion about `beginDispose()`/`disposeFileFallbacks()`/`disposeComposerShapes()` themselves — those are the call sites, and the helper is where the contract lives.
verification: bun install && bun run check:ts && bun test packages/coding-agent/test/disposer-drain.test.ts
gate: All three tests in `packages/coding-agent/test/disposer-drain.test.ts` pass, and `bun run check:ts` is clean. Specifically: (1) run order is `["C", "B", "A"]`; (2) the non-throwing disposer ran AND `logger.warn` fired once AND `drainDisposers` returned normally; (3) the array is empty and the late disposer ran. Additionally a grep must return zero hits for `for (const dispose of` in `packages/coding-agent/src` — proving all four sites were routed through the helper and no fifth forward-order drain was left behind. (That grep is a completeness check on the migration, not a test assertion, and must not be written into the test file.)
gate_can_fail: Yes, three independent ways. A forward-order implementation fails test (1) on the deep-equal. A splice-once implementation fails test (3) on the non-empty array. An implementation with no try/catch fails test (2) on both the run-order array and the fact that `drainDisposers` itself throws. An implementation that rethrows (the chord `throw errors[0]` port) fails test (2) outright. Nothing in the gate can pass on a no-op, because every assertion reads a concrete run-order array or a logger call count. Caveat: the gate's executability currently depends on `bun install` — see plan_corrections; before that, neither `bun test` nor `check:ts` runs at all.
open_questions: A FIFTH teardown-shaped drain site exists that the plan's 'four drain points' does not cover: `clearExtensionTerminalInputListeners()` at `packages/coding-agent/src/modes/controllers/extension-ui-controller.ts:1222-1227` iterates `#extensionTerminalInputUnsubscribers` (a `Set<() => void>`, declared line 85, added line 1203) and then calls `.clear()`. It has the same isolation defect — an `unsubscribe` that throws stops the rest — but a different data structure, so `drainDisposers(list: Array<...>)` does not fit it as written. Decision for a human: in scope for W2 (widen the helper to accept `Set` or convert the field to an Array), or explicitly deferred? The plan's own blast-radius note argues for deferring, since these are TUI input listeners rather than the session teardown chain.

Self-re-registration: the `while (list.length > 0)` loop will spin forever if a disposer unconditionally re-pushes itself. No current disposer does this (all pushes are at agent-session.ts:2179, runner.ts:777 and :796, extension-ui-controller.ts:105, and none are self-referential), so the loop is currently bounded. Should the helper add a defensive iteration cap, or is an unbounded loop that faithfully surfaces a pathological disposer the better failure mode? This is a judgement call, not a defect.

Does this test file need the native addon? The test imports only `drainDisposers` and `logger` — neither pulls in `pi_natives` — so it is EXPECTED to be runnable as soon as `bun install` completes, unlike the rest of the suite. This is unconfirmed because node_modules is absent here. If it does turn out to require the addon, W2 loses its only always-runnable gate and needs a different one; please report rather than working around it.
